claims.statement: The manifest declares the default-SMS-app component contract: an exported SmsReceiver with BROADCAST_SMS and priority-999 filters for both SMS_RECEIVED and SMS_DELIVER, mmslib's PushReceiver and TransactionService for WAP-push MMS, and HeadlessSmsSendService as the required RESPOND_VIA_MESSAGE service; the app gates this behavior on holding the default-SMS role (RoleManager.ROLE_SMS on API 29+, otherwise Telephony.Sms.getDefaultSmsPackage), which MainActivity requests through the system role intent during onboarding.

SMS_DELIVER fires only when the app is the default SMS app while SMS_RECEIVED fires for all apps; when default, SmsReceiver skips SMS_RECEIVED for a PDU already owned by SMS_DELIVER and itself inserts the message into Telephony.Sms.Inbox, whereas as a non-default app only SMS_RECEIVED arrives and the system default app's written row is picked up by the app's content observer.

The system Telephony content providers (Telephony.Sms, Telephony.Mms, Telephony.Threads) are the durable source of truth: SmsReceiver persists the incoming PDU and reads the row back before any fan-out, SmsSender writes outgoing rows into Telephony.Sms.Sent because SmsManager.sendTextMessage does not persist sent messages for non-default apps, and downstream consumers (UI, gateway inbox reads, webhooks) are built from provider state rather than broadcast extras.

MessagesDatabase is the app's local read-SSOT shadow of the providers (v7, eleven entities — the five original plus the five PR-01 durability tables remote_conversation_map, gateway_event_outbox, remote_commands, remote_command_executions, and sync_cursors added purely additively by MIGRATION_6_7); HomeViewModel drives the conversation list from conversationDao().observeAll() Room invalidation only after a read-cutover gate, and a failed shadow (migration/corruption) downgrades to the provider read path instead of killing the app because the shadow is not the source of truth.

SharedPreferences hold gateway/feature configuration: GatewayPreferences owns the sms_gateway_prefs store (enabled intent, runtime mirror, consent version, port, cloud/GMweb settings), and secrets such as the API key and webhook signing secret are persisted encrypted with a non-exportable AES-256-GCM key from the hardware-backed Android Keystore via SecureStore under an enc:v1: marker, so they are never plaintext at rest; the EVE send queue uses a separate eve_queue_prefs store.

docs/architecture-v2-sync.md documents the refactor rationale for the data layer: the old path ran a full dual-source sync, conversation rebuild, and O(10K-rows) unread count on every incoming SMS, and the governing principle adopted is 'If you have the ID, operate on that ID. Full sync is repair, not the main path.'

TelephonySyncCoordinator is the single writer into Room with two channels: exact mutations (Upsert/Delete/RefreshStatus/MarkThreadRead/DeleteThread) processed sequentially without conflation, each Upsert applying message row plus conversation projection in one Room transaction with an O(1) unread delta, while reconcile requests (FullSync/ForThread) are conflated so many nudges collapse into one bounded repair pass.

ChangeRouter converts content-observer notifications into the cheapest shadow update: when the change URI carries an extractable row id it performs a targeted O(1) provider read and mutate (or Delete when the row vanished), and id-less URIs fall back to reconcile, first consulting the LocalProviderWrites hint registry to downgrade a self-caused mark-read to a ForThread repair; all provider I/O is offloaded off the main looper.

IncomingMessageDispatcher is the single fan-out point for all inbound messages and imposes a fixed order: mirror into Room via mutate(Upsert) first — the coordinator commits the durable cloud-event outbox row inside that same Room transaction for a brand-new message — (blocking is a notification policy, not a sync policy — the row stays persisted either way), then, for a non-blocked sender, emit to the SmsEventBus, fire the user-configured local WebhookEngine webhook (best-effort, HTTPS-only, consent-gated — the fire-and-forget cloud upload it used to perform is deleted), and show a notification unless the user is actively viewing that conversation; a blocked sender gets none of the three.

SmsStatusReceiver is manifest-declared (exported=false, no intent filter) so it has manifest lifetime — the SENT/DELIVERED PendingIntent callbacks survive the initiating process going away — and it applies results as a targeted mutate(RefreshStatus) O(1) update instead of a full provider scan, aggregating multipart results before a message leaves PENDING.

GatewayService is the exported=false foreground service (foregroundServiceType dataSync|specialUse) handling ACTION_START/ACTION_STOP/ACTION_RETRY_NOW with START_STICKY, and its ConnectionSupervisor reconcile loop owns the component lifecycles including the LAN GatewayServer, the cloud HeartbeatManager/RegistrationManager, the durable EventUploader that transmits the gateway_event_outbox, the OutboxPoller GMweb pull bridge (started only when gmwebUrl is non-blank), and the data layer's TelephonySyncCoordinator.ensureLoopRunning() so the Room shadow keeps syncing while the gateway is online.

gatewayDesiredEnabled is the persisted user intent that survives reboot and is never touched by runtime teardown; BootGatewayReceiver replays ACTION_START after BOOT_COMPLETED when the intent and consent are present, and every start is re-gated by GatewayAccessPolicy.canStart/canTransmit against stored consent, so a revoked consent silently drops a start and transmission.

All outbound paths converge on SmsSender/MmsSender: the LAN REST endpoints call the senders directly, and both the LAN EVE /send endpoint and the GMweb OutboxPoller enqueue through the persistent priority EveSmsQueue, which GatewayServer wires to send with SmsSender.sendForResult — a single delivery path from every bridge to the radio.

Provider change notifications reach the data layer through SmsContentObserver instances owned by the ViewModels but registered via SmsRepository.registerObserver on both Telephony.Sms.CONTENT_URI and Telephony.Mms.CONTENT_URI; the observer dispatches on the leading edge (first change fires immediately) and coalesces any further changes inside a 150 ms window into a single trailing null-URI nudge, so a burst (e.g. multipart SMS or MMS parts) still ends with exactly one final reconcile.

The ConnectionSupervisor's reconcile loop is itself the gateway's backoff mechanism: a failed reconcile (e.g. a port bind failure) sets State.ERROR and retries after an exponential delay that doubles from 5 s up to a 300 s cap, so the supervisor's start() stays non-blocking and non-throwing while the loop self-heals components in the background.

The durable gateway sync path is live end to end: the single-writer TelephonySyncCoordinator commits each message's cloud event to gateway_event_outbox inside the same Room transaction as the mutation it describes (new upsert, delete, status change, thread read) so the event and the message live or die together, and the supervisor-driven EventUploader is the sole durable transmitter — on start it requeues SENDING rows, gates on prefs.isEnabled and a non-blank gmwebUrl (zero HTTP otherwise), then claims batches transactionally and POSTs them to GMweb applying per-eventUuid partial ACKs; the old fire-and-forget WebhookEngine cloud upload is deleted, leaving only the best-effort local webhook.

GatewayService arms a Doze-safe restart watchdog: on onDestroy it schedules an exact alarm (setExactAndAllowWhileIdle, 15 s out) to replay ACTION_START if the gateway is still runtime-enabled, so the GMweb pull bridge re-arms even when START_STICKY revival is delayed or suppressed by Doze and would otherwise surface to Eve as 503 android_gateway_unreachable.

ConnectionSupervisor owns the gateway's runtime transmission gate: reconcile() clears GatewayPreferences.isEnabled first when tearing down (desired-off or offline) so components stop transmitting, and sets it only after everything desired is up; consumers such as GatewayService.isServiceRunning and the WebhookEngine transmission check read supervisor-derived state rather than a hand-set boolean.
